findings.reason: aj on refreshing tables: after a step, what Java kept up to date differs from what Java answers when the same join is made again from the same rows (runlog/journal.md, 'As-of join: Java's ticking result differs from its own static result': a NaN left stamp joined to a newly added NaN right row under the rule >; for the chains of aj named there see aj-reference-failure). Oxhaven gives the answer Java gives from scratch and agrees with itself. Counted only when Java's two answers do differ for the scenario at hand and Oxhaven's is the one from scratch. Recorded seeds: --ops aj 39, 257, 1319, 1774, 2619.
The same as aj-reference-history, for a table with more differing cells than the comparison lists one by one: the 'truncated' note that ends such a list (recorded seed: --ops aj 675).

The chains of aj of aj-reference-history (PARITY.md, A13; tasks/12.1-fuzzer-coverage.md, F1): an aj with exact match columns whose left table is static and whose right table is a refreshing as-of result. When the right table reports a change that touches neither a match column nor the stamp, Java fails the join in that cycle (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in RightIncrementalHashedAsOfJoinStateManager#addToSequentialBuilder) and serves the rows it had, which earlier runs compared as a match that is gone; since a failed table is compared by its failure alone (PARITY.md, A11) the seeds show as a failure on Java only. Made again from the same rows, Java's join succeeds, and Oxhaven gives that answer. Counted only when Java does answer from scratch for the scenario at hand and Oxhaven's result is that answer. Recorded seeds: --ops aj 2, 465, 540, 675, 1371, 1427, 1735, 2110, 2669, 2873.

aj-reference-failure for raj, which PARITY.md A13 covers since the owner's answer to item 7.19 (tasks/12.1-fuzzer-coverage.md, F1, scenario F1_asof_static_left_right_change_off_its_columns.json): a raj with exact match columns, a static left table and a refreshing right table that is not an input table fails in Java (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in RightIncrementalHashedAsOfJoinStateManager#addToSequentialBuilder) when the right table reports a change that touches neither a match column nor the stamp. Counted only for that shape, and only when Java's join made again from the same rows succeeds and Oxhaven's result is that answer.

PARITY.md A22 (owner item 7.19): Java's vector of a refreshing group_by result is a view of its group, so an aggregation grouped by it, an update_by bucketed by it, a select_distinct of it or a distinct of it fails in the cycle in which a group changes (IllegalStateException: Missing value in probe in IncrementalAggOpenHasherObject; Failed to modify data). Counted only for a table that is, or is made from, an operation that holds such vectors (shape refreshing_group_vectors), and only when Java's result made again from the same rows succeeds and Oxhaven's result holds the rows of that answer: compared as multisets of rows, since an aggregation whose key changed shows the new group at the end, which a table made again cannot (tasks/12.1-fuzzer-coverage.md, F2).

PARITY.md A22 (owner item 7.19): where Java's operation holds vectors of a refreshing group_by result (a distinct of them, or a cumulative or rolling minimum or maximum read by a later operation), it keeps a stale value when the group changes: a distinct keeps the vector it had, and what reads a minimum is not told of the change (tasks/12.1-fuzzer-coverage.md, F2 and F8). Counted only for a table that is, or is made from, an operation that holds such vectors, and only when Java's answer made again from the same rows differs from what it kept and Oxhaven's result holds the rows of the answer made again, both compared as multisets of rows (see group-vector-failure).
group-vector-stale where the stale result has another number of rows (a distinct, or a filter of what reads a minimum): PARITY.md A22, with the same conditions.
group-vector-stale for a table with more differing cells than the comparison lists one by one (the 'truncated' note that ends such a list): PARITY.md A22, with the same conditions.

Counted only for a column made by such an operator and taken apart by an ungroup (shape ungrouped_extreme), with exactly these two sets of metadata.
